classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish sufficient congruence markings from distractors and name matching vertices.

content.prompt: In each part, name the triangle congruent to $\triangle ABC$.

spec.description: Reference triangle with one, two and three side ticks.
spec.mathematics: AC: one tick; AB: two ticks; CB: three ticks.

spec.description: Candidate DEF with two single-ticked sides.
spec.mathematics: DE and EF: one tick; DF: three ticks.
HG: one tick; GI: two ticks; HI: three ticks.

spec.description: Candidate KLM with two single-ticked sides.
spec.mathematics: KL and LM: one tick; KM: three ticks.

answer.worked: $AC=GH$, $AB=GI$ and $BC=IH$ from the matching ticks. Therefore $A\leftrightarrow G$, $B\leftrightarrow I$, $C\leftrightarrow H$, so $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle GIH$ (SSS).

spec.description: Reference triangle with a red dot inside angle B.
spec.mathematics: AB: one tick; BC: two ticks; B: red angle marker.

spec.description: Candidate PRQ with its marked angle at Q.
spec.mathematics: PR: one tick; RQ: two ticks; Q: red angle marker.

spec.description: Candidate STU with its marked angle at T.
spec.mathematics: ST: one tick; SU: two ticks; T: red angle marker.

spec.description: Candidate XYZ with the marked included angle at Y.
spec.mathematics: XY: one tick; YZ: two ticks; Y: red angle marker.

answer.worked: $AB=XY$, $BC=YZ$ and $\angle ABC=\angle XYZ$. The marked angles lie between the matching sides. Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle XYZ$ (SAS).

spec.description: Reference triangle with two angle-marker families.
spec.mathematics: BC: one tick; C: x marker; B: red angle marker.
DP: one tick; P: x marker; D: red angle marker.
NO: one tick; N: x marker; M: red angle marker.
ST: one tick; R: x marker; S: red angle marker.

answer.worked: $\angle ABC=\angle LDP$, $\angle ACB=\angle LPD$ and $BC=DP$. The marked side joins the corresponding marked angles. Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle LDP$ (AAS), with $A\leftrightarrow L$, $B\leftrightarrow D$, $C\leftrightarrow P$.
